_readme: Machine-readable league rules and file map for keeper/draft decisions. Read this before inspecting app source or re-deriving rules from scratch.

league.name: Frank Gore Memorial League y15
league.notes: Superflex league (extra QB-eligible flex slot) with 3 dedicated WR spots. This inflates QB value and WR depth value relative to a standard league; always use league_format.starters, not generic rankings, when judging positional scarcity.

keeperRules.keeperCostExplanation: There is NO round-cost penalty for keeping a player. Keepers simply occupy the last 2 rounds of the current draft (rounds 14 and 15 in a 15-round, 12-team draft). Do not rank/select keepers by 'saved rounds' or draft-cost value — that logic only applies if keeperCost were round-based, which it is not here.
keeperRules.ineligibleDraftRoundsExplanation: A player cannot be kept if they were drafted in round 1 or round 2 of the MOST RECENT draft, regardless of how good they are. This applies even if they were later acquired by another team via trade — eligibility follows the player's most recent draft round, not current roster owner.
keeperRules.priorKeeperSlotRoundsExplanation: If a player was drafted in round 14 or 15, that means they occupied a keeper slot in that draft (i.e. someone kept them). This is a signal, not itself a disqualifier.
keeperRules.maxConsecutiveKeeperSeasonsExplanation: A player can be kept for at most 2 CONSECUTIVE seasons. If a player was drafted in round 14/15 in each of the last 2 straight draft years, they are capped out and cannot be kept again this year — they go back into the general draft pool, no matter how good they currently rank. This must be checked by looking back across draft_history year files, not just the most recent year.
keeperRules.selectionMethod: Since there is no keeper cost, keeper choice should NOT be based on 'value saved vs draft round.' Instead, rank ELIGIBLE roster players (round 1/2 excluded, cap-maxed-out players excluded) by (1) raw current ranking first — trust the market's overall view of talent/risk/role — then (2) valueOverReplacementRounds (this league's actual starter/FLEX/SUPERFLEX counts) only as a tiebreak between players who are close in ranking, then (3) keeperYearsRemaining as a final tiebreak (prefer the player with more consecutive-keeper-season runway left, all else equal). Do not let VOR alone leapfrog a much lower-ranked scarce-position player (e.g. a TE6 or fringe backup QB) over a clearly better overall player just because their position is thin — this was tried and explicitly rejected by the user (Harold Fannin Jr. over Davante Adams, Tyler Shough over D'Andre Swift) as of the 2026 offseason planning.
keeperRules.behavioralNotes: This league's real GMs, per user's direct read of the league (2026 offseason), keep skill-position value (WR2/WR3 tier) over a borderline non-rushing QB1 (e.g. Dak Prescott, Jared Goff, Kirk Cousins) even when the QB ranks a bit higher on paper. This tracks the QB draft-round analysis: this league pays a real round-1 premium for RUSHING QBs (Josh Allen, Lamar Jackson, Jalen Hurts, Kyler Murray all go round 1 nearly every year 2022-2025) but treats pure pocket passers as far more replaceable/skippable, including as keepers. There's no rushing-stat data in the saved rankings file to encode this as an automatic rule, so treat it as a judgment override signal when forecasting opponent keepers for QBs without real rushing production, not something the ranking-based algorithm alone will catch. Confirmed example: 'Look at all those Pickens' locked to keep George Pickens + Rashee Rice over Dak Prescott via keeperLockedOverride in their roster JSON entry. 2026 specific note: 8 QBs kept league-wide (Jayden Daniels, Drake Maye, Matthew Stafford, Bo Nix, Trevor Lawrence, Jaxson Dart, Justin Herbert, Tyler Shough); this makes mid-tier QBs (rank 25-40 range) widely available in draft while mid-tier RBs (RB15-25 range) are much scarcer. Keeper decision should weight RB/position scarcity heavily over raw rank when QB depth post-keepers is this deep.

dataFiles.rankingsSource: STANDARD as of 2026-07-30: straight PPR rankings (data/raw/rankings/FantasyPros_2026_Draft_ALL_Rankings.csv, imported via 'import-rankings-csv'), NOT the old superflex OP file. Top QBs (default top 7) are then nudged up via 'python -m app apply-qb-adjustment', which sets each to the overall pick where a QB of that rank has actually gone in this league's own draft_history (computed fresh each run, not hardcoded) rather than a hand-tuned downward QB shift. This replaced the prior superflex-CSV + board_adjustments.json QB-knockback method for both the post-keeper draft board and keeper selection. See .claude/skills/refresh-rankings/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/keeper-analysis/SKILL.md for the full command sequence, and app/qb_historical_adjustment.py for the implementation. Do not run generic 'combine-rankings' afterward — it re-averages every file in data/raw/rankings/ (including stale superflex/ESPN sources still sitting there) and will overwrite the single-source adjusted rankings_combined.json.
dataFiles.postKeeperDraftBoardNote: Snapshot only — regenerate whenever keepers or rankings change (python -m app keepers-board). Does NOT auto-update.
dataFiles.keeperPreferencesNote: Manual per-team keeper overrides (e.g. known manager intent) — {"Team Display Name": ["Player One", "Player Two"]}. Fills remaining keeper slots ahead of auto-selection; players must still pass eligibility rules. As of 2026-07-30: Wuf (Brock Bowers, Tetairoa McMillan) and AI-ex Gonna Take My Job (Jaxson Dart, Drake Maye) have overrides set.
dataFiles.draftHistoryNote: One file per season: {"year": YYYY, "picks": [{"round": int, "pick": int, "playerName": str, "team": str}, ...]}. Add a new year file after each live draft so the consecutive-keeper-cap math keeps working automatically. Currently have 2020-2025.
dataFiles.draftHistoryRoundCountNote: 2020-2023 drafts were 16 rounds (roster included a kicker slot). Starting 2024, the league dropped the kicker position, so drafts are 15 rounds and PRIOR_KEEPER_ROUNDS (the last-2-rounds keeper slots) shifted from {15,16} to {14,15}. Don't treat a 180-pick 2020-2023 file as complete — it should be 192 (16 rounds x 12 teams); a 180-pick 2024+ file is correct.
dataFiles.draftPicksNote: Which team owns how many picks in each round for a given draft year (accounts for traded picks). Currently have 2026.
dataFiles.standingsNote: Final regular-season standings by team. Draft order for the FOLLOWING season is the inverse of these standings (worst record picks 1st), snaking each round. Use app/standings.py draft_order_from_standings() + snake_draft_order() rather than hardcoding an order. Fetch via 'fetch-standings <year> --league-key KEY' or 'backfill-standings' (requires valid Yahoo OAuth token). Currently have 2024-2025.
dataFiles.nflStatsNote: Player stats from nflreadpy/nflverse (weekly, seasonal, and roster snapshots per season). Used for historical position lookups and player evaluation enrichment. Fetch via 'fetch-nfl-stats [--seasons 2019 2020 ...]. Does NOT include play-by-play (out of scope). Currently have 2022-2025.
dataFiles.draftAnalysisNote: Regeneratable snapshots from draft-analysis reports (e.g. slot vs rank, position vs rank analyses). Optional CSV export via --export-csv flag.
dataFiles.leaguesRegistryNote: Cross-platform league registry (Phase 0 of the multi-tenant roadmap, see docs/roadmap.md). One entry per league: wuff-internal leagueId (this league is 'frank-gore', the default), platform, platformLeagueId, and format (inline or via formatFile pointing at league_settings.json). Regenerate with 'python3 -m app leagues-init --force'; list with 'python3 -m app leagues'.

codeMap.app/strategy.py: Core keeper eligibility + selection logic. Keeper round rules (ineligible rounds, keeper-slot rounds) come from LeagueFormat fields, not module constants. roster_keeper_insight() builds per-player analysis, select_best_keepers() picks the top N per league_format rules.
codeMap.app/league_registry.py: League registry: every league wuff observes across platforms (yahoo/sleeper/espn), loaded from data/config/leagues.json. League dataclass wraps a LeagueFormat; get_league()/load_leagues()/default_league_id(). CLI: leagues, leagues-init.
codeMap.app/draft_history.py: Loads data/raw/draft_history/*.json, computes consecutive_keeper_years() for the cap rule.
codeMap.app/draft_picks.py: Loads data/raw/draft_picks/*.json, who owns which round picks.
codeMap.app/standings.py: Loads data/raw/standings/*.json and derives the next season's snake draft order (worst record picks first, reverses each round). Snake draft, confirmed.
codeMap.app/league_context.py: LeagueFormat dataclass — teams, starters, keeper_cost_uses_draft_round (should stay False), keeper_max_consecutive_seasons, keeper_slots, keeper_ineligible_rounds ([1,2] here), keeper_slot_rounds ([14,15] here). All keeper rules are per-league config now, seeded from league_settings.json.
codeMap.app/roster_store.py: Load/save roster JSON into YahooRosterPlayer objects.
codeMap.app/nfl_stats.py: Fetches and caches NFL player stats from nflreadpy/nflverse: load_player_stats(summary_level='week'/'reg'), load_rosters(). Exposes refresh_nfl_stats() for CLI; load_* functions read CSVs for downstream consumers. Seasons default to FIRST_SEASON (2019) through current_nfl_season().
codeMap.app/draft_analysis.py: Historical draft-outcome analysis: draft_slot_vs_final_rank(), position_in_round_vs_final_rank(). Joins draft_history + standings + nfl_stats rosters to correlate draft decisions with season outcomes.
codeMap.app/cli.py: CLI commands, see README.md for the full runnable list. New in this update: list-league-keys (resolve game_key per season), fetch-standings, backfill-standings, fetch-nfl-stats, draft-slot-outcomes, position-round-outcomes.

teamNames2025Note: Team display names can change year to year even though the 12 manager slots stay the same. draft_history year files store whatever short name was used in that season's draft results — do not assume names are stable across years.
